notes: Built from the breadboard circuit diagram (led1/led2): resistor in series with the LED; long leg (anode) goes via the resistor to GPIO17 (physical pin 11), short leg (cathode) goes to GND (physical pin 20, mapped to GND.4).
Resistor value is not stated in the manual (it points to an LED calculation resource); 220 ohm assumed.
Breadboard positions (resistor 1t.e to 5t.e, LED legs in 5t.d and 6t.d, jumpers in 1t.a and 6t.a) are read from the Fritzing diagram; rows a-e are the top bank 't' in the catalogue naming.
Jumper leads are modelled as male-to-female: male end into the breadboard, female end on the Pi header pin.
The optional 3.3V direct test (led3) and the jumper/solder alternatives for joining the LED and resistor are not modelled.
